subject: Renewal + capacity bump: fixed pricing option and credit structure
messages:
From: Kate Simmons <kate@helionsys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helionsys.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options + capacity uplift

Vivek / team,

Thanks again for the overview yesterday. Quick summary from our side: usage is expected to grow ~35% year-over-year and the product team wants to lock in predictable pricing while we increase committed capacity. Procurement asked if we can get either a short-term price hold while we complete the procurement window OR a renewal that includes a larger commit (we can commit to an additional 30% GPU-hours) in exchange for a deeper discount / credits.

Can you outline what a clean path would look like for Helion — ideally something that shortens legal review and avoids a lengthy amendment loop? We’re targeting a decision by end of month.

Appreciate it,
Kate
Kate Simmons
VP, Cloud Platforms
Helion Systems

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Kate Simmons <kate@helionsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal options + capacity uplift

Kate — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Two pragmatic options that usually work for customers in your position: 

1) 12-month renewal with a step discount + one-time credit: 
   - Commit uplift: +30% base commit over current 
   - Effective discount: 18–22% on per-token/per-embed rates (depending on commit bands)
   - One-time engineering credit: $50,000 applied to next invoice to offset migration/uplift work
   - Standard 30-day legal review (we’ll use our standard renewal exhibit to avoid full contract redlines)

2) Short-term price hold + bridge commitment (6 months): 
   - Fixed pricing hold for 6 months at current rates for current consumption
   - Commit option: we reserve the capacity you need (burst + reserved pool) if you sign a 12-month commit after the hold
   - If you convert to a commit within 60 days: apply a 12% retrospective credit on the hold months

We can attach the pricing summary and a compact SOW for the increased capacity to speed legal. If you want the quickest path to close this month, option 2 is usually fastest: fewer contract changes and we can issue a DocuSign for the hold + procurement addendum.

I’ve attached a short pricing_summary.pdf and a draft MA exhibit with the commit bands. Marissa will follow up on the commercials and Ben can confirm capacity/throughput details.

Next steps: which option do you prefer? If option 1, we’ll send a redline-light exhibit; if option 2, we’ll prepare the DocuSign hold and the conversion clause.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_summary.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Kate Simmons <kate@helionsys.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal options + capacity uplift

Kate — quick commercial clarifications to help procurement: 

- If you take option 1 (12-month renewal), we can ladder discounts by commit tiers: +30% = 20% discount; +50% = 25% discount. We can also front-load a $50k onboarding credit on month 1.
- Overages: billed at 120% of the committed unit rate, but we will cap overage exposure if you convert to a higher commit within the first 90 days.
- For option 2 (6-month hold), we’ll include a unilateral conversion window in the DocuSign that shortens the legal path.

HubSpot deal is updated with the two scenarios: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HLN-2027-05-42. I’ll prepare a one-page summary (Helion_MA_plan_v3.xlsx) you can share with procurement.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Kate Simmons <kate@helionsys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helionsys.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal options + capacity uplift

Thanks — option 2 is more attractive for our finance team because it avoids a lengthy procurement approval cycle. A few procurement asks before we sign: 

- Can you confirm retention of audit logs for 13 months (our policy) and provide a short note on data residency?
- We need a 7-business-day turn on the DocuSign from legal for the hold (legal is constrained this month).
- Please confirm the conversion credit math (12% retrospective credit) and that it applies only to compute token usage, not third-party services.

If you can send a DocuSign with those three calls-out, we should be able to return signed within a week.

Kate

On Mon, Mar 22, 2027 at 10:05 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kate — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Two pragmatic options that usually work for customers in your position: ...

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Kate Simmons <kate@helionsys.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal options + capacity uplift

Kate — quick technical confirmations to support option 2: 

- Audit logs: Redwood can retain control-plane audit logs for 13 months in your region (we’ll include the retention clause in the exhibit). Data plane telemetry (token traces) are sampled; full KV cache data is not stored beyond 30 days unless you enable long-term retention via your Private deployment settings.
- Capacity / autoscale: we’ll reserve a 30% reserved pool and a 40% burst buffer; burst calls will be subject to the overage cap Marissa outlined.
- Conversion: the 12% retrospective credit will be applied to billable compute usage (per-token/embedding units) for the hold months only. It does not apply to third-party licensed components or marketplace fees.

Attaching a short SOW draft (Helion_SOW_draft.docx) and a perf profile to confirm throughput expectations. 

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Helion_SOW_draft.docx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Kate Simmons <kate@helionsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, procurement@helionsys.com
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Finalize: 6-month price hold + conversion path (next steps)

Kate — great, thanks for the quick decision. Summary of agreed next steps and owners: 

- DocuSign: We will send a 6-month price-hold doc with the conversion clause and the three procurement call-outs (13-month audit log retention, residency note, 12% retrospective credit limited to compute). Target: send by EOD 2027-03-30. (Owner: Marissa)
- Legal review: Redwood to accept a 7-business-day review window; we’ll mark the DocuSign as executed on acceptance. (Owner: Legal teams)
- SOW & capacity: Ben to finalize SOW and perf appendix; attach to the DocuSign packet for signing. (Owner: Ben)
- Billing: Once conversion is elected, apply the $50k credit or the 12% retrospective credit per the conversion language. (Owner: Billing)

DocuSign link (will be live in the email you receive): https://docusign.redwood.com/HLN-2027-05-42
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HLN-2027-05-42
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/helion/renewal-pkg

If procurement signs the hold this week we’ll lock the reserved pool and schedule a short onboarding call to validate the burst profile.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to closing this out.
Vivek
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
